items.abstract: OFFICIAL DESCRIPTION OF THE SCIENTIFIC WORK | INTERNATIONAL CATALOG 2026 RESEARCH TITLE: BUILD OR DESTROY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF THE TRANSFORMATIVE POTENTIAL AND DISINFORMATION RISKS OF MODERN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE LEAD RESEARCHER: Dr. Dieudelin Arcangel Legrand - Brotherswagg Robert Academic Jurisdiction and Country of Origin: Republic of Haiti PRIMARY PUBLISHING HOUSE: BrotherswaggStudioRecords Publishing (BSR Publishing) / TM3 MUSIC GROUP INSTITUTIONAL CORPORATE AUTHORSHIP, APPROVAL AND EDITORIAL REVIEW ENDORSEMENT: International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC) and its International Research Consortium: - The Hellenic Institute (Critical Thinking and Theoretical Frameworks) - The Atlantic Research Group (Factual Analysis and Global Perspective) - The Euro-Academic Council (Literary Standards and European Editorial Review) - The Oxbridge Academic (Methodological Rigor and Technical Review) - The Continental Bureau (Source Documentation and Multilingual Research) INTERNATIONAL EDITION: November 2026 ORIGINAL LANGUAGE OF PUBLICATION: Spanish (Official Master Edition) --- 1. SCIENTIFIC CLASSIFICATION AND EPISTEMOLOGICAL NATURE OF THE WORK This publication belongs to the genre of the Critical Review Scientific Article, Epistemological Analysis, and Technological Foresight (an In-Depth Argumentative Scientific Essay). By virtue of its interdisciplinary structure, the work is classified within the fields of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Philosophy of Technology, while establishing direct analytical connections with Communication Studies, Digital Sociology, Applied Ethics, Cognitive Psychology of Perception, and Cyber Law. Having undergone a rigorous process of methodological auditing and structural verification under the standards of the International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC), this research distinguishes itself from conventional technical literature through its comprehensive scope and unwavering commitment to empirical truth. It is neither a merely descriptive manual nor a speculative pamphlet, but rather a reference work designed to diagnose, with surgical precision, the most consequential technological phenomenon of our time. 2. WHY THIS WORK IS ESSENTIAL READING IN THE 21ST CENTURY Humanity is experiencing a historic moment in which the boundary between the real and the artificial has been erased by the speed of algorithms. Every day, millions of people interact with texts, voices, photographs, and video sequences that appear to reflect authentic events but have actually been entirely fabricated by generative artificial intelligence systems. Faced with this unprecedented reality, global society oscillates between two equally dangerous extremes: naïve fascination with the power of machines and uninformed panic in the face of a technology that few people fully understand. "Build or Destroy: A Critical Analysis of the Transformative Potential and Disinformation Risks of Modern Artificial Intelligence" was conceived to dispel this conceptual fog. This work confronts readers with an unavoidable question: How is it possible that the same technology capable of saving lives in medicine, accelerating scientific discoveries, and democratizing education has simultaneously become the preferred tool of countless digital content creators for falsifying reality, impersonating identities, and monetizing deception on a planetary scale? Through rigorous, direct, transparent prose, free from corporate constraints, the Lead Researcher, Dr. Dieudelin Arcangel Legrand - Brotherswagg Robert, together with the IIAEC collegiate body and BSR Publishing, exposes the hidden mechanisms behind this duality without barriers or concealment. Readers who explore these pages will encounter documented truths about how the attention economy operates, why digital platforms amplify synthetic falsehoods, and how society can defend its right to truth without renouncing scientific progress. 3. THE ARCHITECTURE OF THE WORK: AN EVOLUTIONARY NARRATIVE IN FOUR FOUNDATIONAL MODULES To provide a progressive, logical, and deeply enriching reading experience, this research has been structured into seven sections organized around four foundational modules that evolve as one continuous scientific narrative: - FIRST FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | Recent Evolution and Future Horizons of AI: Guides readers from the origins of symbolic computing to the transformer revolution, multimodal foundation models, and emerging autonomous agentic systems, clearly explaining how machines acquired the ability to synthesize realities indistinguishable from the physical world. - SECOND FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | The Constructive and Transformative Potential: Rigorously documents the positive side of this revolution, demonstrating how artificial intelligence is transforming medical diagnosis, drug design, climate sustainability, space research, the inclusion of persons with disabilities, and the democratization of knowledge in every corner of the planet. - THIRD FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | The Anatomy of Deception and a Critical Examination of Malicious Use: Constitutes the critical and revealing core of the manuscript. It examines with intellectual courage how numerous unscrupulous content creators exploit AI to manufacture deepfakes, clone human voices, fabricate pseudo-scientific or pseudo-journalistic evidence, and operate artificial engagement farms, thereby undermining the historical principle of audiovisual evidence and profiting from public credulity. - FOURTH FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | Ethical Discussion, Governance, and the Future of Trust: Proposes concrete solutions to the epistemic crisis by establishing the principles of mandatory transparency, cryptographic traceability from the point of origin, the legal shared responsibility of digital platforms, and the urgent need for critical literacy among citizens. 4. RELEVANCE TO UNIVERSITIES, RESEARCHERS, STUDENTS, AND SOCIETY This work has been conceived as an indispensable reference resource for multiple sectors of the global community: - For Researchers and Academics: It offers an interdisciplinary theoretical framework integrating algorithmic engineering, epistemology, and digital sociology, supported by cutting-edge technical references and international standards. - For Universities and Academic Institutions: It constitutes a bibliographic resource of significant educational value for courses in technological ethics, social communication, computer science, digital law, and contemporary philosophy. - For Students and Young Creators: It provides a moral and technical compass for understanding the power of the tools at their disposal, inspiring them to use artificial intelligence to build genuine knowledge and reject the culture of digital fraud. - For Citizens, Journalists, and the General Public: It delivers the practical and conceptual tools necessary to protect independent judgment against media manipulation and distinguish genuine progress from synthetic illusion. 5. A UNIVERSAL INVITATION: A WORK FOR EVERYONE, BREAKING DOWN BARRIERS AND BUILDING KNOWLEDGE WITHOUT BORDERS Beyond its methodological rigor and technical soundness, this research carries a fundamental declaration of principles: genuine scientific knowledge does not belong to closed elites or intellectual monopolies; it belongs to all humanity. For far too long, the production and validation of global knowledge have been concentrated within hermetic academic canons that erected invisible barriers—geographical, economic, linguistic, and racial—to determine who had the right to conduct research, publish, and be heard. Conceived in the Republic of Haiti with a global outlook and supported by the alliance between BrotherswaggStudioRecords Publishing (BSR Publishing) / TM3 MUSIC GROUP and the International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC), this work deliberately breaks through these historical barriers. It demonstrates that cutting-edge critical thinking, scientific excellence, and the ethical defense of truth can and must emerge from the Global South and reach the entire world, engaging in dialogue on equal terms with institutions across every nation. For this reason, an open, fraternal, and universal invitation is extended to all readers, students, professors, universities, independent researchers, artists, journalists, and citizens of every nation, origin, and circumstance: this work belongs to you. Every page of this study contains essential truths for understanding the world in which we live and defending the future we share. The entire global community is invited to read this article with a critical mindset, debate its arguments in classrooms and across digital networks, cite its findings, translate its message, and actively contribute to the development of an open, inclusive body of scientific literature, free from intellectual racism and committed to human dignity. Because only when knowledge is freed from chains and shared without exclusion does science fulfill its noblest purpose: to illuminate the minds of all human beings. items.title: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests
items.abstract: Coding assistants built on Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a staple of modern software development, increasingly trusted to execute workflows and modernize code end-to-end. Much of this trust rests on passing tests, which are often written by the coding agents themselves. In this work, we examine the ability of these agents to both write reliable tests and translate them between programming languages. We benchmark three popular coding agents, each evaluated with a native frontier model and high reasoning effort. Verifying across a broad suite of metrics, we find that coding agents far exceed human written suites on traditional measures of coverage. This advantage, however, is uneven: agent test quality degrades sharply with project size, and much of the advantage lies in a greater number of written tests. We also show that agentic test translation---while seemingly strong in aggregate---remains inconsistent and unreliable.

items.title: CARDIO-ML-ED Dataset: A Multi-modal Clinical ECG Database for Machine Learning Applications and Data Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives: The CARDIO-ML-ED dataset was collected to address the critical shortage of publicly available cardiovascular databases that integrate electrocardiogram (ECG) imagery with comprehensive clinical metadata. Existing ECG repositories lack detailed patient-level information such as laboratory results, vital signs, and medical history—factors essential for developing clinically meaningful machine learning models. We aimed to create a curated, well-labelled, multimodal resource that supports research in automated ECG interpretation, multimodal fusion, and exploratory clinical phenotyping, while promoting reproducibility and innovation in artificial intelligence (AI) driven cardiovascular care. Data description: The CARDIO-ML-ED dataset comprises two complementary components: (1) structured clinical metadata for 582 subjects, and (2) a curated subset of 408 high-resolution ECG images derived from paper-based records digitized through standardized scanning, normalization, cropping, quality filtering, and noise reduction. The dataset includes 82 clinical features per subject—covering demographics, vital signs, laboratory tests (complete blood count, cardiac enzymes, electrolytes, inflammatory markers, arterial blood gases), and medical history. Diagnostic labels were independently assigned by a cardiologist and an emergency medicine physician, achieving substantial interrater agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.82). This resource offers unique value through its dense integration of ECG data with clinical covariates, enabling multimodal fusion research, unsupervised clustering, imbalanced learning, and predictive analytics.

items.title: Catalysing system reforms in Pakistan’s Healthcare and Health Professions Education: National Stakeholder priorities for strengthening policy and system Governance
items.abstract: Abstract Objective Pakistan has broadened its medical and dental education sphere, yet apprehensions last about undergraduates’ competence, impact of regulation, international acknowledgment of qualifications and retention of the health workforce. This study explored multi stakeholder perspectives on training capacity, quality of education, governance, regulation and acknowledgment of health professions education in Pakistan, and identified prime reforms. Methodology: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using hybrid focus group discussion held on 4 August 2026 as part of national Health and Education Summit Pakistan (HESP) 2026. Fourteen purposively sampled stakeholders participated in discussion guided by 16 semi structured questions. Data were analysed using Framework Method, and Health Policy Triangle was applied as an interpretive lens. Results Nine themes were identified across three domains. Educational quality and competence : undefined and unenforced competency standards; deficits in clinical training infrastructure; faculty development and continuous quality improvement; and cautious, purpose-specific integration of artificial intelligence. Governance, regulation and recognition : fragmented, input-oriented governance; private-sector representation and public–private imbalance; and international recognition and global alignment. Workforce and equity : equity in workforce planning; and workforce sustainability, security and dignity. Participants identified main barrier to reform is not in an absence of policy but in weak implementation, input based accreditation and poor coordination among regulatory bodies. Conclusion Stakeholders called for a shift from input based to outcome-based accreditation built on a nationally agreed definition of competence, a shared inter agency governance platform, documented clinical supervision and simulation, and workforce protection measures.

items.title: Characterisation of Air Quality and Respiratory Health Risks: A Management Framework for a Nigerian Aviation Hub
items.abstract: Airport operational environments generate complex emission matrices that pose severe occupational health hazards, particularly in developing nations lacking systematic surveillance frameworks. This study characterised air quality dynamics at Benin City Airport, Nigeria, and evaluated the associated respiratory health burden among personnel. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was deployed, combining eight weeks of real-time microenvironmental monitoring (CO₂, PM₁₀, PM₂.₅) with an epidemiological survey across 129 eligible airport workers. Significant spatiotemporal variations were detected for particulate matter: the airside zone exhibited peak coarse particle concentrations (PM₁₀: 22.04 ± 0.94 µg/m³) during morning shifts and progressive fine particle accumulation (PM₂.₅) during afternoon shifts, tracking flight operational cycles. Gaseous CO₂ concentrations showed no significant spatial variations across monitoring sites. Respiratory symptom prevalence was high among workers, dominated by chronic cough (57.4%) and shortness of breath (24.0%). Multivariable logistic regression revealed an exposure-awareness paradox: personnel in high-exposure operational zones (Airside and Terminal Halls) experienced significantly higher respiratory morbidity despite reporting higher occupational safety knowledge. Unawareness of safe exposure limits was inversely associated with chronic cough (AOR = 0.38, p = 0.032). High and fluctuating particulate levels create continuous inhalation hazards for frontline personnel. Mitigating these chronic occupational risks requires optimising administrative controls, enforcing mandatory shift rotations, ensuring consistent personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance, and establishing routine environmental health surveillance frameworks.

items.title: Climate change, heat exposure and kidney health in rail construction: H&S implications
items.abstract: Climate change is altering the conditions under which outdoor construction work is undertaken, particularly in rail infrastructure, where physically demanding activities, restrictive personal protective equipment and limited access to welfare facilities can increase heat burdens. Although the health effects of occupational heat exposure are well-established, less is known about how cumulative health risks, including kidney-related risks, are recognised and managed within rail construction health and safety (H&S) systems. This exploratory qualitative study drew on two structured online workshops involving six H&S professionals from construction and infrastructure sectors. Workshop transcripts and notes were analysed thematically. Participants described growing awareness of heat as a workplace hazard, but reported responses that remained inconsistent, reactive and focused primarily on short-term effects such as fatigue and discomfort. Kidney health rarely featured in training, risk assessment or health monitoring. The findings do not establish a causal relationship between rail work and kidney disease. Instead, they identify an organisational gap between emerging occupational-health evidence and current practice. The resulting socio-technical model shows how environmental heat, working conditions, organisational culture and H&S systems influence the visibility of cumulative health risks. This study provides a basis for more integrated monitoring and future longitudinal research in rail construction.

items.title: CliniCIRCA: LLM-powered Clinical Timeline Generation and Summarization from Unstructured EHR Texts for Mental Health Patients
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Mental health care often requires clinicians to reason over patient journeys: longitudinal patterns of symptoms, diagnoses, treatments, behaviors, social context, and responses to care. Yet these journeys are rarely documented as readily available, explicit timelines. Clinically important temporal information is often embedded in unstructured discharge narratives, where events may be repeated, narrated out of order, or expressed through vague and relative time references. This makes temporal recovery difficult for clinicians and computational systems, and can limit the reliability of downstream summarization. Methods: We present CliniCIRCA, a multi-stage large language model (LLM) framework for Calendar-anchored, Imprecision-aware Reconstruction of Clinical Annals. CliniCIRCA decomposes patient-journey reconstruction into three stages: extracting atomic clinical events from raw discharge summaries, assigning calendar-grounded temporal labels with explicit uncertainty, and rendering the verified timeline as a date-grouped clinical summary. The framework is designed to make temporal reasoning inspectable rather than hidden inside a single summarization step. Results: From 14,882 MIMIC-III mental-health-coded admissions, we construct a benchmark of 52 discharge summaries on which CliniCIRCA produces 15,891 temporally tagged events. Following clinician-defined rubrics, human annotation with clinician adjudication corrects 629 errors, producing verified gold-standard timelines. These corrected timelines then drive a temporally grounded summarization stage that compresses each source 1.52 times into a date-grouped chronological record while preserving temporal labels and uncertainty. We further scale the framework to generate 1,000 silver-standard timelines and evaluate them as supervision for smaller open-weight models. Compared with zero- and few-shot prompting, instruction tuning generally improves five open-weight models across event extraction, temporal tagging, and summarization under both silver and clinician-verified evaluations. Conclusions: Auditable temporal reconstruction can serve as both a clinician-readable representation of complex mental health narratives and a reusable supervision source for smaller models. These findings suggest that intermediate, temporally grounded representations may help bridge clinical summarization, timeline generation, and scalable model adaptation, while preserving the need for expert adjudication in high-stakes clinical natural language processing (NLP).

items.title: Co-creating principles for human–AI collaboration: A participatory approach to organizational GenAI integration
items.abstract: This paper examines how participatory sociotechnical approach can support the organizational integration of generative AI (GenAI) in the creative work of a public service organization. Through an exploratory collaboration with the communications department of a Danish municipality, it investigates how employees collectively shape GenAI integration through participatory organizational inquiry and the co-creation of localized sociotechnical principles. The study contributes to design research by providing an empirical account of participatory GenAI integration, extending participatory AI scholarship towards organizational AI integration, and introducing Sociotechnical AI Reflection (STAIR) as a participatory sociotechnical reflection method supporting localized GenAI integration in organizational settings. The findings show that meaningful GenAI integration depends on situated, value-driven processes that reshape professional practice, collaborative work, and organizational learning. The paper contributes to ongoing discussions on how organizations can integrate GenAI in ways that align with professional values, organizational purpose, and creative agency.

items.title: CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
items.abstract: We present CompCert4Lean, a large-scale port of CompCert 3.17's verified compiler core from Rocq to Lean, completed in approximately six weeks by one expert directing parallel LLM agents. Our migration workflow partitions the development along its dependencies, audits translated definitions and theorem statements before large-scale proof reconstruction, and then reconstructs proofs in parallel against stable interfaces. The resulting compiler covers typed CompCert C through x86-64 assembly, discharges all 4,908 recorded proof obligations without project-specific axioms, and produces executable Linux binaries. The workflow enabled the expert to concentrate on organizing the work rather than supplying technical solutions. Of 1,071 human interactions, 88.8% concerned workflow and coordination, while only three supplied technical direction. Optimization campaigns further demonstrate the benefit of the Lean port for agent-driven verified development. Under matched budgets of 24 active hours, GPT-6-astra produced a Lean candidate with 11.7% lower generated-program runtime across 29 small-tests programs, compared with 2.3% lower for its Rocq candidate, both relative to original CompCert 3.17 and while preserving the end-to-end correctness theorem. These results show that parallel LLM agents can support large-scale migration with limited human technical direction and subsequently improve the migrated compiler while retaining its formal guarantees.

items.title: Computing Conditional Shapley Values Using Tabular Foundation Models
items.abstract: Shapley values have become a cornerstone of explainable AI, but they are computationally expensive to use, especially when features are dependent. Evaluating them requires approximating a large number of conditional expectations, either via Monte Carlo integration or regression. Until recently it has not been possible to fully exploit deep learning for the regression approach, because retraining for each conditional expectation takes too long. Tabular foundation models such as TabPFN overcome this computational hurdle by leveraging in-context learning, so each conditional expectation can be approximated without any re-training. In this paper, we compute Shapley values with multiple variants of TabPFN and compare their performance with state-of-the-art methods on both simulated and real datasets. In most cases, TabPFN yields the best performance; where it does not, it is only marginally worse than the best method, at a fraction of the runtime. We discuss further improvements and how tabular foundation models can be better adapted specifically for conditional Shapley value estimation.

items.title: Concisely Explaining the Doubt: Minimum-Size Abductive Explanations for Linear Models with a Reject Option
items.abstract: Trustworthiness in artificial intelligence depends not only on what a model decides, but also on how it handles and explains cases in which a reliable decision cannot be made. In critical domains such as healthcare and finance, a reject option allows the model to abstain when evidence is insufficient, making it essential to explain why an instance is rejected in order to support informed human intervention. In these settings, explanations must not only be interpretable, but also faithful to the underlying model and computationally efficient enough to support real-time decision making. Abductive explanations guarantee fidelity, but their exact computation is known to be NP-hard for many classes of models, limiting their practical applicability. Computing minimum-size abductive explanations is an even more challenging problem, as it requires reasoning not only about fidelity but also about optimality. Prior work has addressed this challenge in restricted settings, including log-linear-time algorithms for computing minimum-size abductive explanations in linear models without rejection, as well as a polynomial-time method based on linear programming for computing abductive explanations, without guarantees of minimum size, for linear models with a reject option. In this work, we bridge these lines of research by computing minimum-size abductive explanations for linear models with a reject option. For accepted instances, we adapt the log-linear algorithm to efficiently compute optimal explanations. For rejected instances, we formulate a 0–1 integer linear programming problem that characterizes minimum-size abductive explanations of rejection. Although this formulation is NP-hard in theory, our experimental results show that it is consistently more efficient in practice than the linear-programming-based approach that does not guarantee minimum-size explanations.

items.title: Content licensing strategy in AI–publisher coopetition: the role of asymmetric comparative advantages and citation intensity
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines strategic content licensing between a generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform and a digital news publisher in digital news markets, an important issue for understanding where AI platforms rely on publisher content while competing for user attention. It analyzes how citation intensity shapes licensing incentives, pricing, user diversion and welfare. Design/methodology/approach We develop a game-theoretic model of two-dimensional horizontal differentiation in which the AI platform has a comparative advantage in content integration and the publisher has a comparative advantage in factual accuracy. The model examines how citation intensity, hallucination risk, user preference correlation and per-use royalty jointly determine equilibrium outcomes. Findings Licensing between AI platforms and publishers arises from a trade-off between two countervailing forces: entry displacement and engagement expansion. Content licensing requires sufficiently high citation intensity; mutual gains additionally require low preference correlation. The pricing effects of citation intensity are nonmonotonic. Subscription prices can rise or fall depending on the strength of citation relative to royalty costs. User diversion is shaped by the balance between referral traffic expansion and direct substitution. Welfare improves only when engagement expansion dominates entry displacement. Originality/value This study models AI–publisher licensing in a two-dimensional Hotelling framework of asymmetric comparative advantages, conceptualizing citation intensity as a content-composition variable that shapes output quality, user traffic and royalty payments beyond existing display-level constructs.
